question.problem:
The area of a square is decreasing at a rate of $48{\text{ cm}}^{2}\text{/s}.$ At what rate is the side of ​​the square decreasing when the side is $4\text{ cm}$ long?

The side is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{cm/s}.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, the area is changing at a constant rate, and we want to know the rate at which the side lengths are changing.

First, let's draw a diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14187261/assets/10e47419775a585e10e732f482ee279bba49d205ee12959cd80c8d33924accbf.png)

We want to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ The area $A$ is related to side length $x$ by the formula

$$
A={x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We know from the given information that

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=-48\text{ }{\text{cm}}^{2}/\text{s}.
$$

Substituting this information, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}-48 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2x \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{48}{2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when the sides are $4\,\text{cm},$ we have $x=4.$ Substituting this information into the above, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{48}{2\cdot 4}=-6.
$$

Therefore, the side is decreasing at a rate of $6\,\text{cm/s}.$
